messages:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU pool 'prod-west-gpu-2' autoscale failed (scale_limit_hit) — queue growth > 5k, throttle:true, impacted routes: /api/v1/generate, /chat. Pager: @Maya @Raj @SRE-Lead :rotating_light:
Maya: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs and current queue numbers.
Raj: ack. moving my laptop to the SRE call. is there an incident runbook for stranded-mig?
Maya: runbook link in #eng-sre pinned. quick summary: MIG fragmentation + heavy binpacking from nightly rebalances caused many 1g slices to be unusable for current large-model requests. autoscaler kept hitting scale_limit and couldn't produce compatible slots.
Emily: seeing 6.2k queued requests at gateway, 99th latency spiking to 9.8s. Throttles active on tier=standard.
Maya: customers starting to see 429s after queue-age exceeded token cutoff. Alex (cust-success): customer reports for two high-traffic apps, one on Dedicated. They say degraded responses since ~12:03 UTC.
Kevin: logs from allocator: `error: no compatible MIG slice for request model=vicuna-13b, required_mem=24G, available_slices=[1g,2g]` lots of `fragmentation` warnings.
Maya: trying quick mitigation: enable temporary routing to fallback-pool (mixed-quant models) for non-enterprise customers to relieve backlog. Raj, can you open a policy override?
Raj: on it. running `rbacctl apply -f /tmp/fallback-route.yaml` — pushing now.
ops-bot: policy-override applied by Raj at 2026-03-15T12:14:02Z.
Maya: immediate drop in queued requests for /api/v1/generate (approx -800 in 30s). good. but Dedicated customers still impacted (private pool pinned).
SRE-Lead: we need to assess stranded capacity in prod-west-gpu-2. run `migctl status --pool prod-west-gpu-2 --format json | jq '.slices | group_by(.size) | map({size: .[0].size, stranded: map(select(.allocated==false and .compatible==false)) | length})'` and paste output.
Kevin: output: 
```
[ { "size": "1g", "stranded": 42 },
  { "size": "2g", "stranded": 8 },
  { "size": "4g", "stranded": 0 } ]
```
Maya: 42 1g slices stranded is huge. looks like recent binpack-rebalance introduced a lot of slab fragmentation. autoscaler can't synthesize compatible capacity because available free slices are mismatched sizes.
Emily: tracing shows many small-model tasks pinned to large 4g slices due to scheduling affinity; that prevented repacking.
Raj: two mitigation paths: 1) manual eviction and repack to create contiguous 24G capacity for vicuna-13b, which will cause live evictions and possible customer impact; 2) MIG resize/slot-coalesce job to merge smaller slices — longer job, needs infra approval. Thoughts?
Maya: escalate to product/CS for Dedicated customer impact if we evict. Alex: what is customer tolerance?
Alex (cust-success): one customer on Dedicated has compliance restrictions — can't be routed to fallback-pool. They will notice evictions. We're coordinating with them, current ask is visibility and ETA.
SRE-Lead: prioritize quick capacity creation with minimal evictions: do a targeted eviction of low-priority batch jobs to free 4x1g contiguous on specific nodes, then request on-demand bake to form 1x4g or 1x24g as needed.
Maya: starting selective evictions now. command: `allocator evict --pool prod-west-gpu-2 --selector 'job.tag=batch-lowprio' --limit 25`
ops-bot: eviction job submitted (job id 7f3a2). progress: 0/25 evicted.
Emily: monitoring node packing metrics — I can run repack for nodes we freed.
Raj: small hiccup: autoscale throttle still preventing instant new node creation due to commit limits. I can temporarily raise scale limit for prod-west-gpu-2 for 15m. Anyone object?
SRE-Lead: do it, set alert for rollback.
Raj: `autoscalectl set-limit --pool prod-west-gpu-2 --limit 48 --ttl 15m` -> applied. ops-bot: autoscale limit updated.
Maya: eviction progress 12/25, we've freed a contiguous run on node compute-17. initiating repack: `repackctl relocate --from node=compute-17 --to node=compute-21 --strategy contiguous`
Kevin: repack job logs: `repack: completed 1/1 target segment consolidated. new contiguous 24G available as 1x24g.`
Emily: scheduling now shows new slot compatible with vicuna-13b. backlog draining slowly.
incident-bot: Impact update: ~2 Dedicated customers affected (one high-urgency), ~12% of total requests saw 429s during peak.
Alex (cust-success): I've notified both customers about mitigation steps and ETA ~15 minutes. they want postmortem once stable.
Maya: good. keep throttles on for non-critical routes and keep fallback routing for public traffic until all Dedicated backlog clears.
Raj: autoscale limit rollback scheduled at 12:34Z.
SRE-Lead: start post-incident action items: 1) investigate root cause: why binpack-rebalance allowed such fragmentation; 2) add preflight checks on rebalance to respect MIG size diversity; 3) run a controlled coalesce job to remove stranded 1g slices overnight; 4) write alert to detect rising stranded-slice ratio > 15%.
Emily: logging action: capturing `repackctl` traces and `allocator` histograms. saving to /artifacts/incidents/1719156789/
Kevin: also capturing node-level MIG configs, candidates for automated coalesce.
Maya: current status: queue reduced to 420 requests, 95th latency 1.2s, throttles still in place. Dedicated backlog down to 4k -> 600 in last 10m.
Alex (cust-success): customer ack: reduced errors, they appreciate the updates, want SLA credit calc later.
SRE-Lead: short post-incident timeline: mitigation succeeded without broad evictions. we did targeted evictions + temporary autoscale limit bump + fallback routing. impact window ~12:03-12:22 UTC.
Maya: assigning owners: Raj -> emergency autoscale guardrails; Emily -> repack/rebalance preflight checks; Kevin -> coalesce automation spec; Alex -> customer comms + SLA calc; SRE-Lead -> write postmortem draft.
Maya: closing the pager for now, we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. if queue >1k again, re-open. :white_check_mark:
